inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K/Annual Report Note (Share Based Payments) and H1-2026 interim Note 11 Share Schemes; SBC is verified small (~$0.06-1.0m/yr) — immaterial relative to reported FCF, unlike the working-capital distortion which dominates

recapitalisation_derivation.description: $40.5m equity raise completed 18-May-2026: $30m rights offer at $0.65/share (1-for-1.53, theoretical max 46.1m shares matching $30m/$0.65=46.15m) with 69% shareholder take-up (31.8m shares) plus F&N Ventures underwriting-shortfall allocation (12.8m shares) = 44.6m rights-related shares, plus a $10.5m strategic placement at $0.65/share = 16.15m shares ($10.5m/$0.65). Total new shares = 31.8+12.8+16.15 = 60.75m. Post-raise shares = 70.526m (Dec-2025 CSV) + 60.75m = 131.28m.
recapitalisation_derivation.net_debt_derivation: Dec-2025 net debt (CSV H1-2026 row) = TotalDebt 58.939 - Cash 10.262 = 48.677m. Raise gross proceeds $40.5m less an estimated $3.0m of transaction/underwriting costs = $37.5m net proceeds applied to bank debt repayment as part of the concurrent refinancing. Post-raise net debt = 48.677 - 37.5 = 11.18m. This is conservative: it does not credit any further H2 FY2026 operating cash generation or additional destocking between Dec-2025 and the May-2026 raise date, which would only reduce net debt further.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: NOT USED — see notes. Base case built bottom-up from FY2026 management EBIT guidance and a mid-cycle margin recovery path, not from historical CAGR extrapolation.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Historical CAGRs are NOT usable growth-rate anchors for this ticker. Revenue and equity CAGRs are dominated by the FY2024-25 impairment/loss collapse ($53.9m impairments, $15.1m inventory provisions, total equity fell from $238.5m FY2023 to $54.9m FY2025, a -52%/yr 2yr CAGR) and by cycle-peak FY2022/23 China Manuka boom years that will not repeat. EPS and 3yr-FCF CAGRs are undefined (sign flips between loss and profit years make CAGR meaningless). This is a cyclical turnaround valued on a mid-cycle earnings anchor (FY2026 management normalised EBIT guidance of ~$15.5m, haircut to ~6.0% EBIT margin in Y1 for execution risk, ramping to ~9.0% by Y10 — still below the FY2022/23 peak of 9.6-10.2% — not on trend extrapolation.
historical_growth.notes: SBC itself is immaterial on this ticker (~0.03-0.5% of revenue historically) so the owner-FCF vs reported-FCF gap from SBC is negligible (~$0.2-1.0m/yr). The dominant distortion in reported FCF is instead a NON-SBC item: inventory destocking. FY2025 reported FCF of +$30.9m included a $46.8m inventory-driven working-capital release (inventory fell $135.8m->$89.0m); stripping that release, FY2025 FCF was actually approximately -$15.9m (-8.3% of revenue). H1-2026 reported FCF of +$20.2m included a further $20.7m inventory release; ex-that, H1-2026 FCF was roughly -$0.5m (breakeven). Carrying either headline FCF margin forward would be a severe and repeated overstatement — this is the single most important modelling trap on this ticker and is why the DCF is built bottom-up from EBIT/EBITDA margins with working capital modelled purely as a function of REVENUE GROWTH (not as a residual of the inventory unwind, which will not repeat once inventory normalises).

wacc_rationale.notes: Base cost of equity 9.0% reflects NZ risk-free (~4.5%) plus a diversified-equity risk premium (~4.5%) for a small NZ-listed industrial/consumer co. Five structural premiums stacked per company-specific risk: (1) NZX micro-cap illiquidity — market cap ~NZ$100m, thin daily volume, +2.0%; (2) extreme cyclicality — EBITDA swung from $33.5m (FY2023 peak) to deep NPAT losses of -$80.4m/-$104.8m (FY2024/25), a peak-to-trough swing far exceeding typical cyclical ranges, +2.0%; (3) China/single-region concentration — historically ~40-45% of revenue from a now-shrinking, cyclically weak market, +1.5%; (4) agricultural/weather and honey-price exposure — biological asset fair values and harvest volumes are weather-dependent, industry-wide oversupply has depressed pricing for multiple seasons with no clear rebalancing catalyst, +1.5%; (5) recent going-concern/covenant-waiver history and execution risk on the FY2026 turnaround — multiple rounds of covenant waivers through FY2024-H1FY2026, a failed $0.80/share takeover, three CEO changes since 2024, and management's own repeated 'subject to execution risk' framing of FY2026 guidance, +1.5%. Total 17.5%, in the high-teens as expected for this risk profile.

bull.narrative: China stabilises faster than expected and North America club-retail momentum continues; FY2026 normalised EBIT guidance of ~$15.5m is met or beaten and margin recovery continues toward the FY2022/23 peak range (9.6-10.2% EBIT margin, here capped at 11.0% terminal to allow modest structural improvement from the cost-simplification program); F&N's Asian distribution relationships accelerate Rest-of-Asia growth; WACC eases 2.5pp as execution-risk and going-concern premiums fade with a clean FY2026 result.

bear.narrative: FY2026 normalised EBIT guidance of ~$15.5m is missed (management has repeatedly flagged 'execution risk'); China consumer demand and distributor destocking continue to weigh on the largest segment with no rebalancing of the industry-wide Manuka oversupply; margin recovery stalls well below FY2022/23 peaks (terminal EBIT margin capped at 5.4% versus FY2025's -15.1% trough, i.e. only a partial recovery); further leadership/governance disruption or a soft FY2026 Manuka honey season pressures results; WACC rises 2.5pp reflecting renewed going-concern-adjacent risk premium.

base.note: Entry price ($0.845) sits ABOVE both current price ($0.755) and base intrinsic value ($0.726). This is a direct, mathematically consistent consequence of the base-case WACC (17.5%) being HIGHER than the 15% IRR hurdle used for entry pricing: discounting the identical cash flow stream at a lower rate (15%) than the WACC used to build fair value produces a larger present value. In other words, on the base case's own projected cash flows, an investor buying at today's price and holding to the terminal year would earn MORE than a 15% IRR (WACC-consistent fair value of $0.726 is only slightly below the $0.755 price, and the return path is such that the 15% hurdle is cleared even a little above the current price). This is the expected direction for a high-WACC cyclical turnaround (WACC > hurdle), the mirror image of the more common growth-stock case where entry price sits modestly below intrinsic value.

sanity_check.notes: Market cap NZ$99.1m and EV NZ$110.3m at current price, matching the brief's expected ~NZ$100m market cap / ~NZ$110-120m EV range. Implied EV/FY2026E owner-EBITDA at current price is ~5.4x (EV $110.3m / FY2026E owner EBITDA ~$20.3m) — a distressed/turnaround multiple, not a growth premium; implied EV/FY2026E owner-EBITDA at the base-case intrinsic value is ~5.2x, both comfortably below the 12x terminal exit-multiple cap used in the DCF, confirming the cap is not distorting the valuation (Gordon growth bound the terminal value in all three scenarios, not the cap). Post-raise book value per share is approximately $0.73 (book equity ~$95.8m [$58.3m Dec-2025 equity + ~$37.5m net raise proceeds] / 131.28m shares), so the current $0.755 price implies a P/B of ~1.03x — a sensible multiple for a company just past a going-concern crisis, neither a distressed discount nor a re-rated growth premium. All three checks (market cap, EV, P/B) are internally consistent with a post-recapitalisation micro-cap turnaround trading close to book value with market-implied EV/EBITDA well inside historical cyclical ranges.

valuation_philosophy.summary: CVT.NZ is valued as a CYCLICAL TURNAROUND, not a growth story. The FY2024 (-$80.4m NPAT) and FY2025 (-$104.8m NPAT) years were catastrophic loss years driven by $53.9m of impairments and $15.1m of inventory NRV provisions during an industry-wide Manuka honey oversupply crisis; FY2022/23 (EBITDA $30.1m/$33.5m) were post-COVID China-boom cycle PEAKS that are not repeatable absent a structural rebalancing of industry supply that has no clear catalyst. Reported recent FCF (+$30.9m FY2025, +$20.2m H1-2026) is NOT a sustainable base — approximately 100%+ of it in FY2025 and effectively all of it in H1-2026 was working-capital release from a one-time inventory destocking program (inventory fell from ~$136m at the FY2024 peak to $68.3m at Dec-2025) that cannot repeat once inventory normalises. The DCF is instead built bottom-up: a FY2026 revenue estimate derived from H1-2026 actuals plus normal seasonality (~$227.7m, still below the FY2023 peak of $234.2m), an EBIT margin anchored to management's own FY2026 normalised EBIT guidance of ~$15.5m (haircut to a 6.0% Y1 margin for the company's own repeatedly-stated 'execution risk' framing, versus the ~6.8% guidance-implied margin), ramping only gradually toward a 9.0% terminal margin that remains below the FY2022/23 cycle-peak range of 9.6-10.2%, and working capital modelled purely as a function of revenue GROWTH (a modest cash use as the business expands) rather than assuming the inventory-release tailwind repeats. A 10-year horizon was used because the margin is still gently improving at Year 5 (6.8%) and only approaches maturity by Year 9-10 (7.2-7.3%). WACC was stacked to 17.5% (high-teens) reflecting NZX micro-cap illiquidity, extreme historical cyclicality, China/single-market concentration, agricultural/weather exposure, and the company's own recent going-concern and covenant-waiver history. The result — base-case intrinsic value of $0.73 against a $0.755 current price (-3.8% downside) — is a legitimate and expected outcome for a recapitalised turnaround trading near fair value on recovery hope rather than a screaming bargain or an obvious short; the market appears to already be pricing in a reasonable central-case recovery. Bull ($1.30, +72%) and bear ($0.29, -61%) show the wide dispersion of outcomes typical of an early-stage, execution-dependent turnaround, and the FY2026 result (due 28-Aug-2026, only ~2.5 weeks after this valuation date) is a binary near-term catalyst that could move the stock materially in either direction before the base case's own assumptions can be tested.
